Nina K.: Quick question — my spouse's child is 28 and recently became permanently disabled. Can we add them as a dependent to medical outside open enrollment?

Asha (People Ops): Hi Nina 1 Congrats on getting that sorted at home. Short answer: possibly. Adding an adult dependent due to new permanent disability is usually treated as a QLE by most carriers, but there are specific docs we need and carrier rules vary.

Nina K.: What docs do you need exactly? We have a recent SSA determination letter and a letter from their neurologist. They live with us and we financially support them.

Asha (People Ops): Good start. Typical requirements:``
- SSA determination letter confirming disability (date and status)
- Physician statement with diagnosis and expected permanence
- Proof of dependency/support (tax return showing dependent status OR 3 of: shared lease, joint bank statements, utility bill with their name, proof you provide >50% support)
- Government ID (passport or state ID) for identity verification``
Some carriers also ask for the effective date of disability. If the SSA determination date is within the carrier's QLE window (usually 30 days of the decision), you can submit for a midyear enrollment.

Max (Benefits Ops): Adding: also confirm that the plan's definitions allow adult disabled dependents past age limits (most do when they meet disability criteria). Send documents via the benefits portal under "Dependent Disability Verification" and include the SSA letter date and the date they started living with you (if different). Link: https://benefits.redwood.example/upload

Lina (Payroll): One note on payroll: if enrollment is approved retroactive, deductions will be adjusted and we might issue a balancing payroll entry. If effective date is future, deductions start the next payroll after the effective date. Expect a one-pay-cycle lag for the deduction to settle in the system.

Nina K.: Ok uploading now. Any special redaction rules? Their SSN is on the SSA letter.

Asha (People Ops): Please redact full SSNs in uploads. Last four is fine. For the SSA letter we accept a redacted copy plus a screenshot of the SSA portal showing the determination with your name and case ID.

Asha (People Ops): Yes, most carriers have an internal appeal. We'll coordinate documentation and a formal appeal if needed. If you want, I can pre-fill the appeal outline so the carrier has everything up front.
